chunks: Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Sulayman ibn Dawud or one of our companions, from him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man from your mawali died and left behind young children, and left some property, and upon him was a debt, and the creditors do not know about it. If it is paid to his creditors, his children will remain, and they will have nothing.' So he said, 'Spend it upon his children.'
ai.seo_question: How is debt handled when a deceased person leaves behind minor children and limited property?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS), the jurists derive a principle of prioritizing the welfare of dependents (dhurriyyah) when the estate is insufficient to cover both debts and maintenance. This reflects the Shia legal preference for balancing the rights of creditors with the preservation of the family's livelihood, ensuring the children are not left destitute while the debt remains unsettled. The hadith highlights the flexibility in applying debt repayment when the estate is small, contrasting with stricter interpretations that might prioritize creditors exclusively.
